messages.author: 4883757c9ed610ed
messages.subject: rstan error Issue for new user
parts:
I am very new to Rtan and I have some problems with it, I hope someone can help me out with my little project.

I try to similate the following factor model in rstan:

R=BF+e, where R is an N by1 vector, B is NxK vector of scaled covariances, F is the unobserved Kx1 factor . e is normally distributed with mean 0 and covariance matrix sigma.(particularly, I used identity matrix as the covariance matrix)

Here's my rstan code:

library("rstan")

model1code<- 

 'data{
    int<lower=1> K; 
  
    int <lower=1> N;

    vector[N] R;
  

}

  parameter{

    vector[N] epsilon;

    matrix[N,K] beta;

    matrix[K,N]  beta_t;  
    
    vector[K] F;

}
 
  transformed parameter{

    mu0 <- beta_t*F+epsilon;
    
  
    sigma0  <- beta*F*beta_t;

  }



  model{

   F ~ normal(0,diag(K));  # assign the prior
   beta ~ normal(0,100);     # each entry in matrix beta is normally distributed with N(0,100)
   beta_t ~ normal(0,100);  #the transpose of beta
   epsilon~normal(0,diag(N));  
   R ~ normal(mu0, sigma0);
}'
   R<-rnorm(100,0,1)
   N<-100
   K<-100
 test_dat <-  list (N= N, K= K,R =R )

fit <- stan(model_code=model1code, data= test_dat, iter=1000, chains = 4)

print(fit)

the following error happened:
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'model1code' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=11, column=3

  parameter{
  ^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Parser expecting: <model declaration

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstan error Issue for new user
parts:
On Friday, May 29, 2015 at 2:08:19 PM UTC-4, Jia Qi Xiao wrote:
Thanks for the reply, could you explain it in more detail? I'd like to know how to fix the error

You wrote

parameter{ # singular

vector[N] epsilon;
   matrix[N,K] beta;
   matrix[K,N]  beta_t;  
   vector[K] F;
}
transformed parameter{ # singular

mu0 <- beta_t*F+epsilon;
   sigma0  <- beta*F*beta_t;
}

and you got a parser error

  parameter{
  ^-- here

which indicates something is wrong at or near that line. What is wrong is that parameter and transformed parameter are not valid names for Stan blocks. The correct names are the plural forms parameters and transformed parameters. So, you should write

parameters{ # plural

vector[N] epsilon;
  matrix[N,K] beta;

//  matrix[K,N] beta_t; # not a parameter
  vector[K] F;
}
transformed parameters { # plural
  vector[N] mu0;
  matrix[N,N] sigma0;
  {
    matrix[K,N] beta_t;
    beta_t <- transpose(beta);
    mu0 <- beta_t * F + epsilon;
    sigma0 <- beta * F * beta_t;
  }
}

I rewrote it a bit because beta_t should not be a separate unknown from beta.

Ben
